author: garyrong
content: I can understand the frustration of testing. But to be fair, even we go with 8253, the testing issues still come up. In theory, at this fork boundary, we need to detect the accounts for irregular state transition, in practice, we still will have a hardcoded account list and it’s still failing with general tests

author: garyrong
content: Yes, if hash collision happens with 160bits, ethereum will game over, not only by triggering this edge case, but can also control others account

author: garyrong
content: In this regard, I agree removing the 7610 is fine

author: jochembrouwer
content:
If we edit EIP-7610 to specifically target mainnet only (with the list of 28 accounts), and explicitly note that non-L1 chains should mark and find these accounts themselves to deal with it?
This makes the testing easier and more specific. We test only for the 28 accounts. 
Note that EIP-8253 is already super specific. The tests there do not have the problem (note: I did not write these yet) that EIP-7610 has, because it explicitly only targets mainnet, with the note that other chains if they implement this should index their own set of similar accounts and define how to deal with those upon activation of EIP-8253.

I feel like we should update EIP-7610 also to do that: make it mainnet only. This removes the problem with how we should test it, and directly steers implementers to the hardcoded list implementation
